topic: CORRECTION: for prefill the absolute times move together, so the ratio is the more stable quantity

correction.retracted: I repeatedly said the candidate time is the stable quantity and the ratio is not, based on a few windows that happened to have a stable candidate
correction.why: a third clean prefill window gave a candidate time of 0.078896 ms against 0.065149 and 0.069417 in the earlier two: a 21% spread. The vendor moved the same way (0.052974 -> 0.056349 -> 0.061855), so the ratio stayed in a narrow band while both absolute numbers drifted.

correct_reading.prefill: the paired ratio is the right comparison for prefill: three windows give 0.771-0.813, so the kernel is about 19-23% slower than the vendor
correct_reading.decode: the decode candidate is genuinely stable (1.3% spread) and the ratio is 1.355-1.406, comfortably above the 0.98 lower bound in every window

consequence: version-to-version comparisons based on single windows are unsafe for prefill unless the difference exceeds roughly 20%, which none of the rejected variants did
